rationale: Confirmed against the source: each reachable vertex is settled once and each of its adjacency entries is scanned once. Strictly improving relaxations cause at most E+1 heap entries, each push/pop costing O(log(E+1)); initialization and traversal add O(V+E). Time is O(V+E log(E+1)). The costs map and visited set use O(V), and the lazy heap can hold O(E), giving O(V+E) auxiliary space. Module-level demonstration calls are outside the dijkstra entrypoint.

Each branch reduces the active interval to about one third: the lower third, middle third, or upper third. Thus the loop takes O(log n) iterations. The fixed precision tail examines at most 9 elements. The iterative entrypoint uses O(1) auxiliary space. This review covers ite_ternary_search only, not the separate recursive implementation.

assumptions_override: For nonempty strings of lengths m and k, the method fills the m×k interior of a table allocated with (m+1)(k+1) cells. An empty input returns in O(1). Character comparison/indexing are O(1). Let n=max(m,k); the coarse O(n²) class is a valid upper bound for all lengths and is tight when m and k are comparable. Exclude the returned substring from auxiliary space.
rationale: For nonempty inputs, every one of the m×k interior DP cells is processed, so time and auxiliary space are Θ(mk). The returned substring uses O(min(m,k)) space but is output and excluded; the table dominates. Empty input returns in O(1). The coarse O(n²) class with n=max(m,k) is an upper bound even for unbalanced lengths, and is tight when lengths are comparable.

The implementation allocates and fills an (i+1)×(W+1) table, doing constant work per cell. With i≥1 and W≥1, time and auxiliary space are O(iW), and the coarse n=max(i,W) class is O(n²). The scalar result and input arrays are excluded.

assumptions_override: Analyze sort on a valid DAG represented by its existing adjacency lists. All referenced labels exist; label hashing/comparison and HashMap lookups are expected O(1); adjacency iteration is linear in degree. Analyze a fresh graph with WHITE vertex colors and exclude the returned LinkedList from auxiliary space. The sort mutates colors, so repeated calls require resetting/rebuilding graph state. Deep graphs may overflow the Java call stack.
rationale: DFS colors each vertex once and checks each adjacency entry once; expected O(1) map calls and O(1) linked-list front insertion preserve O(V+E) time. Excluding the returned list, the recursion stack alone is O(V) auxiliary space. The graph’s vertex colors are mutated; run with fresh WHITE state. Deep recursion can overflow the Java stack.
